newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA, Reichmann project worth more than $100 mln.
newsitem.headline: ICA, Reichmann project worth more than $100 mln.

text.p: Mexican builder Empresas ICA and Reichmann International will invest more than $100 million in building an office tower in Mexico City, an official at the Mexican firm said on Thursday.
"The project is worth slightly more than $100 million....It will begin next July and should be completed by December 1999," a high-ranking official at ICA's financial department told Reuters.
"We are going to finance this along with Reichmann; for our part we will use our own money," added the official, who wished to remain anonymous.

Reichmann International, a venture between the families of Canadian real estate magnate Paul Reichmann and billionaire financier George Soros, and ICA announced the deal earlier this week, but gave no details.
The ICA official said the so-called Chapultepec Tower would be 55 floors tall and located on Mexico City's plush Reforma Avenue, a tree-lined boulevard that is comparable to Paris' Champs Elysees.
The tower will combine some commercial space with state-of-the-art offices, he said.
The project is evidence the Mexican economy is on the mend following the 1994-1995 peso crisis, the official said.
"The Chapultepec Tower had been planned for 1995 and it was abandoned because of the crisis -- neither we nor Reichmann were willing to do it with high interest rates at the time," he said.
"Now that the economy is better, we both thought it was the time to restart the project," he said.
